newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - London and Frankfurt hit new peaks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - London and Frankfurt hit new peaks.

text.p: London and Frankfurt stocks soared to new peaks in early trade on Tuesday, lifted by a blistering overnight rally in New York which drove Wall Street to a record close.
But on currency markets the dollar was subdued as traders digested German economic data and awaited the outcome of Britain's monthly monetary meeting, unexpectedly brought forward from Wednesday.

Most of the action was in equity markets. London, reopening after a public holiday on Monday, roared above the 4,500 level on the FTSE index for the first time. Frankfurt started trade at a record high. But Paris fell, held back by political uncertainties.

The engine driving the big advances in Europe was New York's performance on Monday where stocks hit record territory on hopes that a balanced budget agreement would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates again later this month.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 143.29 points, or 2 percent, to 7,214.49, beating the old mark of 7,085.16 set on March 11 and its 16th record so far this year.

"It was almost like a tidal wave coming," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. It was one of the biggest point gains ever for the 30-share average and other market averages also set records
The momentum sent London's blue-chip FTSE index to 4501.1 points at the opening, eclipsing the previous intra-day high of 4468.4, set on May 2.

Shares fell back slightly by mid-morning on worries about interest rates as the monthly monetary meeting between the new finance minister Gordon Brown and Bank of England governor Eddie George was brought forward to Tuesday.
"Sellers in the futures knocked the market back and there's a few sellers in on the back of the rate meeting," said one trader. "But I think the market is now steadying up."
The Treasury said Brown will make a statement at 1000 GMT on the outcome of the meeting. Analysts interpreted the move as a sign that interest rates are set to rise.
Analysts were forecasting a quarter point rise in UK base rates.

"A quarter point is unlikely to upset anyone," said one equity salesman. "Perhaps more important is the possibility of a rise in U.S. rates...and we have another six weeks to wait before the new government's budget."

In Frankfurt, stocks advanced to 3584.56 points near the opening, beating the previous trading high of 3533.18 set only yesterday amid a a batch of positive corporate news reports and New York's strong performance. "All the news has been positive today," said a Frankfurt dealer. "Wall Street was good, the Nikkei was better and we are simply keeping up."
The bullish mood also spread to Madrid and Brussels where stocks hit fresh peaks in early trade. Paris opened higher but quickly fell by 0.5 percent.
Political worries over the May-June general election were keeping investors edgy with opinion polls on Monday showing an advance for either the left or the right.
On Currency markets, the dollar was steady but quiet in early trading as traders awaited the outcome of Britain's monetary meeting.

The dollar retreated from overnight highs against the mark and the yen amid some fresh optimism about economic activity in Germany and Japan but traders said there was little net change in the U.S. currency from Monday's levels.
"The dollar's pretty flat from yesterday's close and looks well supported around current levels," said Ian Gunner, economist at Chase Investment Bank.
The dollar was at 1.7280 marks in early transactions compared with 1.7286 late on Monday.

Details of the April German unemployment report leaked out on Monday and proved broadly in line with the official data released early Tuesday. Seasonally-adjusted jobless rose 8,000 during the month, with a drop in the unadjusted unemployment rate to 11.3 percent from 11.7 percent in March.
Earlier, the April German Purchasing Managers Index reinforced a view of a recovering German economy.

Despite the rise in German economic activity, jitters about an interest rate rise in Japan are more pronounced and the yen gained against both the dollar and mark overnight while Japanese government bond yields pushed higher.
STOCKS PRICES AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 25.7 points at 4,481.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 20.62 points at 2,652.22.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 40.35 points at 3,569.13.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7280 marks compared with 1.7286 marks late in Europe on Monday. It was at 125.68 yen, compared to 126.62 on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $342.80 an ounce, compared to Friday's close in London of $340.05. Silver was $4.76.
